_about: Hand kept, not generated. The content audit's Content Graph (15 September 2026) found 63 records that are one thing recorded under two ids (finding content-003): every same_entity_as edge the graph computed is a title or Arabic match, checked in noor-content-graph.json before it was copied here. This file keeps only the pairs where the two records really are one entity written twice, so scripts/graph/build_graph.py can stamp a `canonical` id on every node (step 19b). It leaves out the pairs where a Path chapter retells a prophet's, a place's or a word's story under a matching name (17 chapter pairs in total, among them chapter:9 and prophet:ibrahim, chapter:43 and place:p-hunayn): a chapter is its own stop on the discovery path (Short, Light, the word, the person or place, the Path chapter, the sources), not the same record as the thing it narrates, so its id is never folded into another's. Keys are the alias, values the id the alias stands for; a companion or a place outranks its own dictionary word, an angel written in characters.js outranks the same angel written again in unseen-data.js, and where neither exists the remaining record stands alone. No id in a source data file is renamed by this batch; only the graph's own `canonical` field changes. Rebuild candidates the same way build_graph.py does (its same_entity_as edges, excluding any pair that touches a chapter: id) if the collections change; add a pair here only once it is verified by title or Arabic against the source files, never guessed.
